name: Physlib Refactoring Report: Refactored Space, time derivatives, the electromagnetic field strength and the tensor API, and sped up the slowest files
description: Physlib Contribution Report on work by Zhi Kai Pong: “Refactored Space, time derivatives, the electromagnetic field strength and the tensor API, and sped up the slowest files”.

issuer.name: Physlib Contributions
issuer.description: An open-source community project to digitalize results from physics into Lean 4. Physlib Contributions publishes signed reports on reviewing, maintenance, refactoring, foundations, formalisation and documentation of Physlib.

credentialSubject.narrative: Replaced the Space d.succ convention by Space d throughout the library and simplified the curl and distributional Laplacian definitions. Replaced the field strength matrix by index expressions on the field strength tensor and reworked the tensor API it depends on. Rewrote the slowest declarations after profiling the whole library, and replaced a home-grown number type by its Mathlib equivalent. Introduced derivVec, the time derivative of trajectories into torsors, and switched the rigid-body and pendulum velocities to it; made the differentiability API of the electromagnetic potential and fields usable by fun_prop.

achievement.name: Physlib Refactoring Report
achievement.description: For changing the structure of existing Physlib code without adding new results: generalising definitions, merging duplicate definitions, reorganising files, or speeding up compilation, so that later work is easier.

criteria.narrative:
- The change restructured existing Physlib code rather than adding new results.
- The change was merged and leaves the library easier to use or extend.
- Links to the relevant pull requests are given as evidence, with a short account of what changed and why.
